title: Domination by point blowups at regular surface points
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact, meaning every open cover has a finite subcover). Let $T\subseteq X$ be a finite set of closed points such that $\mathcal O_{X,t}$ is a regular local ring of Krull dimension $2$ for every $t\in T$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] whose restriction over $X\setminus T$ is an isomorphism. There exist $n\geq0$, a sequence $X_n\xrightarrow{b_n}\cdots\xrightarrow{b_1}X_0=X$, and a morphism $h:X_n\to Y$ such that $f\circ h=b_1\circ\cdots\circ b_n$. Each $b_{i+1}:X_{i+1}\to X_i$ is the blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] in the reduced closed subscheme consisting of a single closed point $p_i\in X_i$ whose image in $X$ lies in $T$. The empty sequence is permitted.

proof.text: Put $U=X\setminus T$. It is open because $T$ is a finite union of closed points. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], $U$ is quasi-compact; by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], $X$ is quasi-separated. Together with the assumed quasi-compactness of $X$, these are the base and open hypotheses for elimination of indeterminacy.

source.place: Tag 0AHI, first sentence of the proof, checking the hypotheses of flat.tex Tag 081T; properties.tex Tags 01OW, 01OY and 01OZ.

proof.text: Properness of $f$ includes separatedness and finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $Y\times_XU\to U$ is an isomorphism by hypothesis. Apply [sk-lem-nagata-sketch-elimination] with base $X$, open $U$ and morphism $f$. It gives a $U$-admissible blowup $b:B\to X$ such that the strict-transform map $g:Y^{\mathrm{st}}\to B$ is an open immersion and $b^{-1}(U)$ is schematically dense in $B$. Unpack [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]: there is a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$, with $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$, and an identification $B\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ over $X$.

source.place: Tag 0AHI, first sentence; flat.tex Tags 081T (lemma-dominate-modification-by-blowup) and 081S (lemma-zariski-after-blowup), with the preliminary dense-open blowup included.

proof.text: By [def-nagata-strict-transform] and [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure], $Y^{\mathrm{st}}$ is a closed subscheme of $Y\times_XB$. The projection $Y\times_XB\to B$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] makes its composite $g$ proper. In particular $g$ is a closed map by [def-weil-proper-morphism], so its image is closed. That image contains $b^{-1}(U)$: the open over $U$ used to form the strict transform maps isomorphically onto $b^{-1}(U)$ because $f$ is an isomorphism there. Its complement must be empty. Indeed, on an open $V$ disjoint from $b^{-1}(U)$, schematic density makes $\mathcal O_B|_V\to0$ injective, forcing every local ring on $V$ to be zero, so $V=\varnothing$. Thus $g$ is surjective. By [def-weil-open-immersion], an open immersion identifies its source with its open image, hence $g$ is an isomorphism. Compose $g^{-1}:B\to Y^{\mathrm{st}}$ with $Y^{\mathrm{st}}\to Y\times_XB\to Y$ to obtain $q:B\to Y$. The fibre-product square gives $f\circ q=b$.

source.place: Tag 0AHI, reduction to an ideal blowup; flat.tex Tag 081T, last two sentences, including the details omitted there; morphisms.tex Tags 01W4 and 01W5.

proof.text: For $x\notin T$, the equality $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$ says $(\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I)_x=0$. Hence $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I)\subseteq T$. Apply [lem-per-surface-point-ideal-principalization] to $(X,T,\mathcal I)$: its Noetherian, finite-closed-set and regular-local dimension-two hypotheses are exactly those of the item, and its ideal hypothesis is supplied by Step 2. It gives a finite tower $X_n\to\cdots\to X_0=X$ of blowups at single reduced closed points mapping into $T$, and $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{X_n}$ is an effective Cartier ideal and in particular invertible. Write $t:X_n\to X$ for the composite.

The image quotient $t^*\mathcal I\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal I\mathcal O_{X_n}$ is the canonical quotient defining the extended ideal [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. Its image is invertible by Step 4. The final-object assertion of [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property] therefore gives an $X$-morphism $a:X_n\to\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)=B$, so $b\circ a=t$. Set $h=q\circ a$. Then $f\circ h=(f\circ q)\circ a=b\circ a=t$, as required. The point centres and their images in $T$ are those already furnished in Step 4. The argument permits the length-zero tower; in particular if $T=\varnothing$, one can take $n=0$ and $h=f^{-1}$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q27-465a863a6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all five steps and every cited statement against Stacks 0AHI, 081S/081T, 0AHH and 0806. The item's statement matches 0AHI hypothesis by hypothesis, and the empty tower is allowed. Step 1: U is open and quasi-compact by the Noetherian open-subscheme leaf, and X is quasi-separated by the locally-Noetherian leaf. Step 2: all hypotheses of the 081S elimination node hold. Its 'first chosen' schematic-density wording is harmless, because b^-1(U) is dense anyway: points of T have 2-dimensional local rings, so they are not generic points. Step 3 writes the details 081T omits. g is the closed subscheme of Y×_X B followed by a base change of a proper map, so it is proper by clause (b) of the closed-immersion node. Its closed image contains the dense set b^-1(U), so the open immersion g is surjective and therefore an isomorphism. The schematic-to-topological density argument is correct, and f∘q=b checks. Step 4: Supp(O_X/I)⊆T, and the 0AHH node's hypotheses match exactly; it gives a tower at reduced closed points over T with I·O_{X_n} invertible. Step 5: the extended ideal plus the final-object property (0806, as stated in its blueprint_update) give a, with h=q∘a and f∘h=t. Edge cases checked: T empty (n=0, h=f^-1), X empty, extra components of Y, non-integral X, and the plane blown up at a point. There are no new nodes. My DAG search for 081T/0AHI and dominate/blowup terms found no duplicate, and there is no cycle (closure of 273 nodes). No SGA source is used. I accept the tool_uses for the 081S elimination node and the 0806 universal-property node. Maintainer note: the main statement of thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property is self-referential (an inherited base fault); its blueprint_update carries the content used here.
